body.v: Your inbox is 99% full. Sign in within 1 hour, or new emails will be rejected.

hotspots.explain: "cl0uddrive": a zero replaces the o. And even spelled correctly, it would not be CloudDrive's domain, clouddrive.example.
"Dear user": the service that runs your account knows your name.
That one-hour deadline: who set it, you or them? The threat of losing emails is there to rush you.
The button leads to cl0uddrive-support.example, a lookalike domain. When you hover over it, a lookalike address can look perfectly normal.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone posing as CloudDrive. "cl0uddrive" has a zero instead of the o, and it is not CloudDrive's domain anyway.
choices: Someone with an almost identical address

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: Fear and haste: if you do not act within the hour, you will lose emails.
choices: Fear of losing emails, within the hour
None, it is a routine notice

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Sign in through the link. Your login details would go to the sender.

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Click nothing. Report the email to the IT team, then check your mailbox by opening the official site yourself.
choices: Reply to ask whether the message is genuine
Open the official site yourself and report the email
Hover over the link and sign in if it looks right

actions.label: Click nothing, report it to the IT team, then open the official site yourself
actions.consequence: Your mailbox is working normally. The email was fake, and your report may spare a colleague the same trap.

actions.label: Sign in through the link, quickly
actions.consequence: The page looks like CloudDrive, but your login details go to the scammer.

actions.label: Reply to the sender to ask whether the message is genuine
actions.consequence: "Of course," the scammer replies. And now they know your address is active.

actions.label: Hover over the link and sign in if the address looks right
actions.consequence: A lookalike address can look perfectly right. Your login details are gone.

attacker_reveal: You read "clouddrive". There was a zero where the o should be, and an hour on the clock so you would not look too closely. People worried about their inbox read words, not letters.
